News & Analysis on Domestic and International Trade, National and State Finances, Budget, Government Regulation, Monetary Policy, RBI Rates, Interest Rates, CRR, Indian Trade, Monetary and Industrial Policy.

item.title: Finmin pegs Q2 expansion at 7.35%,flags capital pressure over US yield
item.description: India’s economy is estimated to have grown 7.35% in the September quarter, supported by strong industrial output, GST collections, energy use, port traffic and auto sales, the finance ministry said. It expects domestic demand and investment to sustain momentum, while warning that high crude prices, food inflation, rupee pressure and elevated US bond yields could pose risks in the second half.

item.title: IMF flags Super El Niño risks to India’s growth, says impact yet to materialise
item.description: According to the IMF, India continues to act as a significant growth engine within the global economy. Despite looming threats posed by weather phenomena like Super El Nino, these risks have yet to materialize. Recent adjustments have raised growth forecasts to 7 percent for the fiscal years 2027 and 2028, reflecting robust domestic demand and a thriving service sector.

item.title: India can achieve $1 trillion exports target this fiscal despite global headwinds: Piyush Goyal
item.description: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal expressed confidence that India would achieve its $1 trillion exports target in 2026-27 despite global uncertainties. He said nine FTAs could open preferential market access to economies with a combined GDP of $60 trillion. Goods and services exports were estimated at $476.2 billion in April-September.

item.title: FICCI names Sanmar Group Chairman Vijay Sankar President-Elect for 2026-27
item.description: FICCI has appointed The Sanmar Group Chairman Vijay Sankar as its President-Elect for 2026-27. Currently the industry body's Senior Vice President, Sankar will succeed Anant Goenka as President after the FICCI Annual General Meeting and Annual Convention scheduled for November 18-19, 2026, in New Delhi.

item.title: AI and data analytics to power next phase of government audits, says CAG
item.description: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India aims to enhance audits by adopting advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence and machine learning. This integration will allow for more precise identification of risks and anomalies in public governance. Data-driven audits will improve the overall efficiency and effectiveness of the auditing process. CAG intends to create a technology-enabled, citizen-centric institution, providing timely and reliable government accounts.

item.title: US trade deal will protect all sensitive Indian interests, says Piyush Goyal
item.description: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said India’s trade deal with the US would protect sensitive interests, including those of farmers, and give the country a competitive advantage. He criticised opposition parties for questioning the agreement before its details were released, while defending India’s trade strategy and its decision to stay out of RCEP.

item.title: Government should support both job-creating and frontier industries: EAC-PM chairman Dev
item.description: S Mahendra Dev highlighted the importance of supporting job-creating and frontier industries for future economic growth. He mentioned that sectors like textiles and technology can significantly enhance India's industrial landscape. The need for improved competitiveness and product quality in various firms was also emphasised. Furthermore, land availability and global supply chain shifts present unique opportunities for India. Overall, addressing these challenges is crucial for the country's industrial transformation ahead.

item.title: Abolish LTCG, rationalise STCG, STT rates on equities: PHDCCI to Finance Ministry
item.description: PHDCCI has recommended abolishing Long Term Capital Gains tax and modifying short-term capital gains taxes. The chamber suggests increasing the holding period for long-term investments to attract genuine investors. It emphasizes that current tax structures discourage investment due to double taxation on equities. Foreign Portfolio Investors have withdrawn significant funds from Indian equities, impacting investment levels. Government analysis of these recommendations may lead to changes in tax policy and structure.

item.title: Finance ministry estimates India’s Q2 FY27 GDP growth at 7.35%
item.description: The finance ministry’s nowcasting model estimates India’s GDP will grow 7.35% in Q2 FY27, following 7.8% growth in the previous quarter, supported by stronger industrial output, energy consumption, port traffic, GST collections and automobile sales.

item.title: Govt extends Amnesty Scheme under ESIC for three month till December 31
item.description: The ‘New Amnesty Scheme 2025’, rolled out on October 1, 2025, is a one-time dispute resolution initiative aimed at reducing the backlog of court cases and promoting compliance under the erstwhile Employees’ State Insurance Act. Court cases filed up to March 31, 2025 are eligible under this scheme, the ministry said on Thursday.

item.title: Central Asia's biggest state makes renewed push for infrastructure & AI projects
item.description: Kazakhstan President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev outlined plans to strengthen energy security, expand infrastructure, develop artificial intelligence and improve living standards in his October 28 state-of-the-nation address.

item.title: IIT Kharagpur and Absolute launch Smart Scout AI project for soybean farming
item.description: Absolute and IIT Kharagpur are developing an early warning system for soybean farmers to minimize crop losses. The Smart Scout project aims to detect lodging risks, assess damage, and estimate yields using artificial intelligence. This initiative is part of the Quad-backed AI-ENGAGE program focusing on agricultural innovations. Pilot trials will be conducted across major soybean-growing states in India over the next three years.

item.title: Can Asia keep growing as oil and debt bite? IMF’s Krishna Srinivasan explains
India will gain strong comparative advantage after US trade deal: Piyush Goyal
item.description: Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal highlighted India's potential advantages from a trade deal with the United States. He asserted that the agreement would not harm the interests of farmers or any other stakeholders involved. Goyal made these statements during the 4th ISID-IDRA National Conference in Delhi. The trade deal aims to enhance India's economic landscape and strengthen its global standing.

item.title: India is addressing Wall Street’s favourite ‘elephant’ in the room to its own advantage
item.description: The Indian government has identified 762 potential applications of artificial intelligence across 62 ministries and departments, spanning farming, railway safety, tax compliance, public grievances, customs and healthcare. While some tools are already in use, others remain in pilot or development stages.

item.title: '2026 resembles 1991': CEA Nageswaran says India is at a critical economic inflection point
item.description: Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran emphasized that 2025-26 could be a significant inflection point for India's economy. He mentioned the challenges posed by global shocks and supply-side disruptions in recent years. The reliance on imported crude oil adds to India's vulnerability to fluctuating international energy prices. Strengthening resilience to external disruptions is crucial for managing such risks effectively.

item.title: India-US trade facilitation portal records 3,500 registrations, says Piyush Goyal
item.description: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal announced that the Trade Facilitation Portal has received about 3,500 registrations. This portal aims to facilitate greater trade opportunities for Indian businesses, especially among micro, small, and medium enterprises. Goyal emphasized that the initiative will help first-time exporters establish partnerships and access new markets. The encouraging response to the portal indicates its potential to expand the global reach of Indian businesses.

item.title: EPFO plans to invest in startups, AIFs five years after govt approval
item.description: The Employees Provident Fund Organisation is working on guidelines for investing in alternative investment funds for better portfolio diversification. The proposed allocation could be up to 3% of fresh annual accretions to these funds. This decision follows recommendations for EPFO's participation in the Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0. Proposed safeguards will include limits on individual fund exposures and minimum corpus requirements.

item.title: SKUAST VC proposes green cess for tourists and research cess for orchardists at Apple Conclave of CII in Kashmir
item.description: In a bid to boost revenue in Jammu and Kashmir, Nazir Ahmad Ganai has proposed a green cess targeting tourists with the aim to fund horticulture research through a suggested research cess levied on orchardists. Leading experts gathered to explore ways to capitalise on Kashmiri apples, emphasising advancements in branding and cold-chain logistics.

item.title: Union Cabinet approves ₹10,000 crore Container Manufacturing Scheme to boost India's production
item.description: The Union Cabinet has approved significant schemes to enhance India's manufacturing infrastructure and capacity. The ₹10,000 crore Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme aims to increase container production substantially by 2040. Additionally, the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana will be implemented from 2026-27 to 2030-31, providing crucial funding. The Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme will also support sports equipment production from 2026 to 2034.

item.title: Government extends PLI scheme for textiles until 2033-34 to boost MSME participation and investments
item.description: The government has announced an extension of the Production Linked Incentive scheme for the textiles sector until 2034. This change aims to encourage more companies to participate by relaxing eligibility norms for investment. The textiles ministry has reduced the minimum turnover requirement for certain manufacturers from ₹200 crore to ₹100 crore. A reopened application portal will accept submissions for manufacturing various textiles from November 1 to December 31.

item.title: Union cabinet approves 3% DA hike for 11.6 million central employees and pensioners, effective July 1
item.description: On Wednesday, the Union cabinet approved a 3% increase in dearness allowance for employees and pensioners. This increase is expected to benefit over 11.6 million individuals ahead of the festive season. The change will take effect retrospectively from July 1, costing the exchequer ₹10,016 crore. Additionally, the government revised dearness allowance rates for employees under the Fifth and Sixth Pay Commissions.

item.title: Manjhi releases 1,000 crore under PM job scheme to support 11,333 micro enterprises
item.description: Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises minister Jitan Ram Manjhi announced the release of ₹1,000 crore in subsidy. This funding aims to support 11,333 new micro enterprises while facilitating bank credit of ₹3,260 crore. The initiative is anticipated to create over 1.02 lakh sustainable employment opportunities, primarily in rural areas. The subsidy is part of the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme, designed to boost grassroots entrepreneurship.

item.title: Green financing in India rises to $82 billion, but flows mostly to established sectors: Report
item.description: The Landscape of Green Finance in India, now in its fourth edition, maps actual finance flows or disbursements across sources, instruments, sectors, and subsectors for financial years 2022-23 and 2023-24. According to the report, while green finance has increased substantially between 2016-17 and 2023-24, financial flows remain concentrated in established sectors and technologies.

item.title: Heat-related deaths up 36% since Paris Agreement: Lancet
item.description: The report, which was released on Wednesday, said the annual average heat-related deaths rose by nearly 36% globally after the Paris Agreement was introduced. "In 2023 alone, heat was linked to a record 710,000 deaths with more than 70% of that toll attributable to human-caused climate change," it said.

item.title: New GST registration route allows online sellers to expand using ecommerce warehouses as local bases
item.description: Starting November 1, small online sellers will have a new option for GST registration. They can use ecommerce warehouses as local bases in other states, promoting nationwide sales. This initiative is part of a broader effort to simplify regulations and reduce expansion costs for small traders. Eligible sellers must meet specific conditions, including tax liability limits and operator consent.

item.title: IIP growth eases to 4-month low in September as mining output contracts
item.description: September witnessed a decline in India's factory output growth, falling to 6.7%, the lowest rate observed in four months. The drop is largely linked to a high base effect and decreased mining activity. Despite this, manufacturing output surged by 7.6% compared to the previous year, while electricity generation also grew, spurred by robust demand even with insufficient rainfall. Economists anticipate GDP growth to surpass 7% for the July-September period.

item.title: Centre releases Rs 78 crore for senior citizens' welfare scheme
item.description: The ministry said it has released funds under the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPSrC), a component of the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), for the financial year 2026-27.

item.title: Karnataka, DGFT to host state-level workshop to help exporters leverage FTAs
item.description: On October 30, a workshop will be organized by the DGFT, Karnataka government, and FIEO in Bengaluru. The event aims to enhance Karnataka's export competitiveness and awareness of Free Trade Agreements. Nearly 200 participants, including exporters and industry officials, are expected to attend. Technical sessions will cover opportunities in various sectors and policy interventions under new FTAs. Senior officials and the state minister will address attendees at this important event.

item.title: PM Modi to release Rs 18,680 crore under PM-Kisan scheme on October 30
item.description: On October 30, Prime Minister Narendra Modi is set to launch the 24th installment of the PM-Kisan scheme in Gujarat, aiming to support over 9.34 crore farmer families across the country with more than Rs 18,680 crore. In Gujarat alone, financial assistance surpassing Rs 1,051 crore will be granted to over 52.33 lakh farmer families.

item.title: India only major emerging economy set to reduce debt ratio by 2031: RBI Deputy Governor
item.description: India is projected to be the only emerging market economy among nine economies with gross domestic product (GDP) exceeding USD 1 trillion to reduce its government debt-to-GDP ratio between 2025 and 2031, Reserve Bank of India Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta said, highlighting the country's stronger fiscal position amid rising global debt and borrowing costs.

item.title: Union Cabinet approves Rs 7,395 crore for PM Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana
item.description: Union Cabinet has allocated Rs 7,395 crore for the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana. This scheme will promote local-level capacity building and resource management for panchayats across India. Elected representatives will receive training to enhance their governance capabilities and local planning efforts. The initiative aims to financially empower panchayats through better utilization of available resources. Implementation will occur from 2026-27 to 2030-31, aligning with the Sixteenth Finance Commission period.

item.title: Cabinet approves Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme with outlay of over Rs 1800 crore
item.description: The Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme has been approved by the Union Cabinet to develop the sports goods industry. The initiative includes creating dedicated Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones to enhance production capabilities. Significant financial support is allocated to encourage innovation and research in sports equipment manufacturing. The scheme aims to generate new employment opportunities and reduce import dependency in this sector.

item.title: India, Mexico begin talks for trade pact; aim to boost commerce, investments
item.description: India and Mexico have initiated negotiations for a preferential trade agreement to enhance bilateral trade and investment. The agreement aims to create new economic opportunities while addressing market access, customs procedures, and trade facilitation. Discussions included organising a Mexican business mission to India in early 2027 to improve commercial ties. India had a trade surplus with Mexico, largely due to exports in autos and pharmaceuticals.

item.title: Centre open to changes in DPDP law to protect press freedom, says Ashwini Vaishnaw
item.description: The Centre aims to amend the Digital Personal Data Protection law to address concerns raised by news publishers. Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw stated that the law does not limit press freedom. This response follows a Supreme Court notice regarding a petition from the Digital News Publishers Association and others. Publishers argue the lack of exemption for journalism could jeopardize investigative reporting and confidential sources.

item.title: India's industrial growth slows to 6.7% in September from 8% in August
item.description: India's Index of Industrial Production for September recorded a growth rate of 6.7%. This figure represents a decline from August's 8%. Key contributors to this growth include the manufacture of motor vehicles and electrical equipment, among others. The manufacture of rubber and plastics also played a significant role in September's performance. These statistics were released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.

item.title: Cabinet hikes Dearness Allowance by 3% with Rs 10,000 crore allocation; check key announcements
item.description: DA hike: The Union Cabinet has approved several development schemes totaling Rs 29,267 crores for various initiatives. Among these is a Rs 10,016 crore increase in Dearness Allowance for Central government employees. The DA will benefit about 48 lakh employees and 68 lakh pensioners, with hikes effective from July 1, 2026.

item.title: India's soybean imports surge to record as domestic prices rally
item.description: India's soybean imports significantly increased to 1.1 million metric tons in 2025/26 compared to the previous year. Rising domestic prices prompted Indian mills to enhance their overseas purchases of soybeans. The majority of these imports originated from Niger, which became the largest exporter to India.

item.title: GST clarification on foreign investor brokerage offers sentiment boost, analysts say
item.description: The Indian government has clarified that brokerage paid by overseas clients may qualify as an export service. This could help foreign investors avoid the 18% goods and services tax on brokerage fees. Analysts suggest this clarification is sentimentally positive amid significant foreign outflows from Indian stocks. There is ongoing speculation regarding potential cuts in capital gains tax ahead of the federal budget.

item.title: India, Mexico sign terms of reference to kickstart trade pact negotiations
item.description: India and Mexico have signed the Terms of Reference to initiate negotiations on a Preferential Trade Agreement. This agreement aims to enhance bilateral trade and investment opportunities between the two countries. Key negotiating areas include market access, customs procedures, and trade facilitation measures. Both delegations discussed organizing a Mexican business mission to India in early 2027.

item.title: India, Azerbaijan move to reset ties, boost energy investments and connectivity
item.description: Delhi and Baku are currently taking steps to improve bilateral relations through enhanced economic cooperation and connectivity initiatives. After a positive meeting, the Foreign Ministers of both nations emphasized the importance of the International North-South Transport Corridor. There has been a notable increase in Indian investment in Azerbaijan's energy sector, with cumulative investments reaching $1.26 billion. Additionally, both countries are working to strengthen security cooperation against transnational crime.

item.title: India’s record bank cash surplus fades as RBI curbs rupee bets
item.description: Indian banks have seen their excess funds drop significantly as the Reserve Bank of India maintains liquidity tightness. This monetary policy is aimed at curbing speculation against the rupee, which has reached critical levels. The central bank has provided limited liquidity support and capped assistance at 1.5 trillion rupees. Consequently, overnight borrowing rates have risen close to the top of the monetary policy range.

item.title: India in striking distance of 8% growth as reforms boost economy: Shaktikanta Das
item.description: Das said the BFSI sector has a crucial role to play in India's journey from a lower-middle-income economy to a high-income economy, through its intermediation in allocation of financial resources. He said the sector would be required to support India's next-gen Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), be the frontline of green and transition finance and become the catalyst for democratising financial inclusion to support this journey.

item.title: GST registration gets easier as CBIC drops Udyam proof, sets seven-day limit for approvals
item.description: The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs has issued clarifications regarding GST registration requirements for businesses. Companies will no longer need to provide Udyam certificates or face rejections due to unpaid bills. Registration applications must be processed within seven working days with Aadhaar authentication. Tax demands must include clear justifications and cannot be arbitrary. These changes aim to simplify compliance and reduce disputes in tax administration.

item.title: Centre eases GST rules for post-sales discounts, no prior agreement needed from November 1
item.description: The Centre eases GST rules on post-sales discounts from November 1, no longer requiring a prior agreement, which is expected to help FMCG and pharma companies and retailers.

item.title: India to emerge as major exporter to China, ASEAN, get edge in US trade pact, says Piyush Goyal
item.description: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal highlighted India's potential to expand exports to China and ASEAN. Negotiations are underway for a trade pact with the United States that could provide India a comparative advantage. The country is also working towards an Investment Protection Agreement with the European Union. Goyal indicated that discussions for preferential trade agreements are progressing with multiple countries and groups.

item.title: Government mulls simplifying application process under Press Note 2 to ease FDI flow from border nations: Sources
item.description: The government had relaxed FDI restrictions imposed under Press Note 3 for countries sharing land borders with India, such as China and Pakistan, through Press Note 2 in March.

item.title: Russia’s farm exports to India rise 11% in nine months, led by sunflower oil
item.description: Russia's agricultural exports to India rose significantly in the first nine months of the year. Agroexport reported shipments reached 1.3 million tons, primarily driven by sunflower oil. This represents an 11% increase in volume compared to previous figures, amounting to $1.45 billion. Trade between India and Russia has expanded significantly, growing more than 20% overall this year. Both countries aim for $100 billion in bilateral trade by 2030.

item.title: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra urges states to ensure quality spending, prudent borrowing
item.description: Addressing the 36th conference of state finance secretaries at the Mint Road, Malhotra appealed the states to onboard onto the Unified Lending Interface (ULI) and utilise Programmable Central Bank Digital Currency (P-CBDC) for Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT).

item.title: India considers measures to boost local production of 100 critical inputs to cut import reliance, government official says
item.description: India is taking steps to encourage the local manufacturing of 100 key items that are currently imported. This initiative aims to decrease dependence on foreign suppliers, especially from China, to enhance domestic production capabilities. The government has identified these crucial items from a broader import list valued at $51 billion, which includes various sectors. By reducing reliance on imports, India hopes to strengthen its economy and mitigate supply chain risks.
